findings.title: Blocklist lookup is case-sensitive, so case variants of a blocked address bypass it
findings.description:
`should_block?` runs an exact `where(email: email)`. The value comes from the signup form. `UsersController#create` builds the user with `User.new_from_params` (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:160), which assigns `params[:email]` unchanged (app/models/user.rb:87), and nothing in `User` normalizes email before validation. The validator passes that raw value through (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13). PostgreSQL `=` is case-sensitive, so an entry for `bad@spamclub.com` does not match `Bad@spamclub.com` or `bad@SpamClub.com`.

The project normalizes emails on lookup in several places (`Email.downcase` in app/controllers/session_controller.rb:17, app/controllers/users_controller.rb:269, app/models/invite.rb:20). But `Email.downcase` only lowercases the domain (lib/email.rb:21), so reusing it would still miss local-part variants. Most mail providers treat the local part case-insensitively, so a block list should compare fully lowercased addresses. Normalize in `should_block?` and on write (a `before_validation` on `BlockedEmail`), or match with `lower(email) = ?`. Add a spec that signs up with a mixed-case address against a blocked entry.

findings.title: `should_block?` writes to the database during validation, so each blocked signup is counted twice and the counter is racy
findings.description:
`should_block?` increments `match_count` and saves on every call (lines 13-17). It is called from `EmailValidator` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:13), which runs on every `valid?` and every `save`. `UsersController#create` calls `user.valid?` (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:168) and then `user.save` (line 172), so one blocked attempt increments `match_count` by 2. The spec at spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb:29 checks `.by(1)` per direct call, so it does not catch this.

Two smaller issues in the same method. `match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a read-modify-write, so concurrent requests lose increments; use `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(...)` instead. And line 18 returns `nil` rather than `false` when nothing matches, which breaks the predicate's boolean contract. Consider a read-only `blocked?` check in validation and recording the match in the controller after a failed save.

findings.title: Invite redemption for a blocked address raises `RecordInvalid`, and the invite can never be redeemed
findings.description: `create_new_user` calls `User.create_for_email` (line 47), which uses `user.save!` (app/models/user.rb:103). A blocked address now raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, and nothing on the path rescues it. `InvitesController#show` calls `invite.redeem` (app/controllers/invites_controller.rb:12) with no rescue. `ApplicationController`'s `rescue_from Exception` (app/controllers/application_controller.rb:38-48) reports the error and re-raises, so the user gets an unhandled 500. The `Invite.transaction` in `InviteRedeemer#redeem` rolls back `redeemed_at`, so every retry fails the same way. Invite validation (app/models/invite.rb:23-33) does not check the blocklist, so such an invite can be created. The domain-restriction setting already has this failure mode; the blocklist extends it to individual addresses. Check blocked status when the invite is created, or rescue `RecordInvalid` in `redeem` and redirect to `/` as the other failure branch does.

findings.title: Tests miss the new behavior and the new response contract
findings.description:
- The validator spec stubs `BlockedEmail.should_block?` entirely (lines 11 and 17), so the database-backed path, mixed-case input, and the double count are not exercised. The negative example (lines 10-14) uses `stubs` without an expectation, so it passes even if the validator never consults the blocklist.
- `spec/controllers/users_controller_spec.rb` has a `.create` block starting at line 285 with no failure-path example for the new `errors` and `values` keys (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:195-200), and none for a blocked-email signup.
- No JS test covers the `rejectedEmails` flow. `test/javascripts/controllers/` contains only `topic_controller_test.js`.

findings.title: The inline message for a rejected email is wrong
findings.description: `emailValidation` returns `user.email.invalid` for every address in `rejectedEmails` (lines 69-74). Entries come from any `result.errors.email` (lines 274-275), including "has already been taken" and the blocklist message "is not allowed." The inline text is "Please enter a valid email address." (config/locales/client.en.yml:216), which is false for a well-formed address. The server message is also flashed, so the user sees two contradicting messages. Store the server reason alongside the email, or use a neutral inline reason.

findings.title: `rejectedEmails` is shared across instances and grows without bound
findings.description: `Em.A([])` inside the `extend` hash is created once and shared by every instance of the controller. This is harmless only because Discourse keeps a single instance; initializing it in `init` avoids the problem. Line 275 pushes on every failed submit without de-duplication. If the email field was blank, `result.values.email` is `null` and that gets pushed too. `addObject` plus a non-empty check fixes both.

findings.title: The blocked-signup response tells unauthenticated clients that an address is blocklisted
findings.description: The blocked message (config/locales/server.en.yml:734, "is not allowed.") goes back in `errors` and the flash (app/controllers/users_controller.rb:195-200). It is distinct from the domain-restriction message (server.en.yml:733), so a spammer can probe which addresses are listed. Honeypot failures get a fake success instead (users_controller.rb:158, 351-359). If you want to hide the list, do the same here. This is a design tradeoff, so it is noted rather than flagged.

findings.title: Moving the domain-restriction logic out of `User` preserves behavior
findings.description: `User#email_validator` and `User#email_in_restriction_setting?` were removed. A repo-wide search finds no remaining references. The whitelist and blacklist behavior is still covered through `valid?` in spec/models/user_spec.rb:488-561. The validator now also performs the blocklist write, so it has two jobs; the second finding covers that.

findings.title: Minor style inconsistencies in the validator
findings.description: Line 13 uses `and` where the codebase uses `&&` (for example app/models/user.rb:561). The file has no trailing newline (line 24).

findings.title: Migration matches the model
findings.description: `email` is NOT NULL with a unique index, which backs the `presence` and `uniqueness` validations on `BlockedEmail`. `action_type` is NOT NULL with no database default, and the `before_validation` callback fills it in. The repo has no `db/schema.rb` or `structure.sql`, so no schema dump needs updating.

findings.title: Response shape matches the JS consumer
findings.description: The `errors` hash (from `to_hash`, keyed by attribute) and the `values` hash (`name`, `username`, `email`) match the fields read at app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:274-275. `values` includes only the three submitted fields, so no password data is echoed back.
